scenario: WIBTA for lying to my brother for the rest of our lives about having a disorder? | My brother who is 2 years younger than me has Aspberger's. We have known for years but it's not something that we talk about in my family because my brother is embarrassed of it in a way. He is EXTREMELY smart and always has been. He excels in math and physics and everything in between. He is going to college and taking hard classes that he does well in. Lately, he has been depressed. More than depressed. A couple of months ago, he tried to take his own life by getting drunk and swallowing a bottle of acetaminophen. He and I are extremely close and he only talks to me. He called me in a panic hours after doing this and I took him to the hospital. He went to outpatient treatment after getting discharged from inpatient. The nurse had called me and asked if my brother was diagnosed with autism ever because he shows some clear signs. I talked to my brother about it today and he is still somewhat denying that he has autism. My brother loves me to death and I love him just as much. He has always looked up to me. I can't imagine a world without him. He loves how much more alike we get as we get older. He constantly says it with a big smile on his face. I have tried to talk to him about his autism and how he shouldn't be ashamed and he should own that about himself because some people don't even realize he has bad communication skills and he's so damn smart. Occasionally, his bad communication skills are very apparent and his disorder is obvious in other ways as well. I try to tell him that people say Mark Zuckerberg and Steve Jobs have Aspberger's but it doesn't do much for him when I say that. I feel if I tell my brother I have Aspberger's as well he would learn to love it and not deny it anymore, possibly helping himself. Would I be an asshole if I live a lie for the rest of my life to make my brother feel he's not alone and possibly help him move forward in life?

Lately, he's been really depressed, even to the point of attempting suicide a couple of months ago. He called me in a panic, and I took him to the hospital. After that, he went through outpatient treatment. The nurse at the hospital mentioned that he shows signs of autism, which made me talk to him about it again. He's still denying it, but I know he's struggling with his self-image. I love him so much, and I can't imagine life without him. I want to help him feel better about himself, especially since he's so smart and capable but sometimes has communication issues that make his disorder more apparent. I thought maybe if I told him I have Asperger's too, he might feel less alone and stop denying it. But I'm wondering if that's a good idea. Would lying about having the disorder make me a bad person? I want to help him, but I don't want to cross any moral lines either. Let me break this down. First, the intent: I want to support my brother and help him feel better about himself. That's a good intention. But the method is lying about having a disorder I don't actually have. Is that acceptable? I know that honesty is generally important in relationships. If I lie, it could damage our trust in the long run, even if my intention is to help. On the other hand, if telling him I have Asperger's helps him accept his own diagnosis and feel less alone, maybe it's worth it. But I'm not sure if that's the case. I should also consider the potential consequences. If he finds out I lied, he might feel betrayed, which could harm our relationship. Plus, lying can create more problems than it solves. It might prevent him from seeking the right help or understanding his own condition properly. Another angle is the impact on me. If I lie, I might feel guilty or stressed about maintaining that lie. It could affect my mental health, which in turn could affect how I support him. I also wonder if there are other ways to help him without lying. Maybe encouraging him to talk to a therapist or join a support group where he can meet others with similar experiences. That way, he doesn't feel alone, and he's getting genuine support. I should also think about how he might react if I told him I have Asperger's. Would he believe me? If he does, would it help him accept his own diagnosis? Or would it confuse him more? I'm not sure. In the end, I want to do what's best for my brother. But I'm torn between wanting to help him and maintaining honesty. I need to weigh the potential benefits against the risks of lying.
